subtopics.title: Water the Puller-Apart — Ions in Solution

questions.question: Water is described as a polar molecule because:
options: It carries a full negative charge overall
Its oxygen corner is slightly negative and its hydrogen corners slightly positive
It freezes at zero degrees Celsius

questions.question: When copper sulfate dissolves, the hydrogen faces of the water molecules turn toward:
The correct dissolution equation for magnesium chloride is:
A dissolution equation passes its charge audit when:
options: Only the atoms balance on each side
The right-hand side carries more positive than negative charge
Every ion is written without a charge
The charges on the right sum to the charge on the left — zero for a neutral solid

questions.question: In the conductivity tester, a glowing bulb proves that the solution contains:
options: Mobile ions acting as charge carriers

questions.question: Sugar solution leaves the bulb dark because sugar dissolves:
options: As whole neutral molecules that carry no charge

questions.question: Doubling the amount of salt dissolved in the beaker makes the bulb:
options: Go dark, because the ions collide
Glow brighter, because the concentration of charge carriers has increased

questions.question: Conductivity cannot serve as a general measure of solubility because:
options: A very soluble substance like sugar can produce no ions at all

subtopics.title: Precipitation — When Two Clear Solutions Make a Solid

questions.question: A precipitate is best described as:
options: A gas that bubbles out of a mixture
The colour change in a solution
An insoluble solid that forms when two solutions mix
The water that evaporates from a beaker

questions.question: The balanced equation for mixing barium chloride and sodium sulfate solutions is:
In that reaction, the sodium and chloride ions are called spectator ions because they:
options: Stay dissolved and unchanged in the water throughout
Change their charges during the swap

questions.question: According to the Grade 10 short-list, which pairing would precipitate out of solution?

subtopics.title: The Ion Test Kit and the Four Reaction Types

questions.question: After nitric acid, silver nitrate produces a cream precipitate. The ion in the sample is:
A white precipitate with barium nitrate that persists in dilute nitric acid identifies:
Nitric acid opens every ion test because it:
options: Destroys carbonate first, so it cannot fake another ion's white precipitate
Speeds up the mixing of the solutions

questions.question: A neutral magnesium atom becomes a Mg²⁺ ion during a reaction. The reaction type is:
options: Redox — the atom changed charge because electrons were transferred

questions.question: The two faces of a water molecule are:
options: A north pole and a south pole
A slightly negative oxygen side and a slightly positive hydrogen side
Fully charged plus and minus ends

questions.question: When salt dissolves, its ions are:
options: Levered off the crystal and wrapped in escorts of water molecules
Left behind as a grey powder

questions.question: Sugar's disappearing act differs from salt's because sugar molecules:
options: Split into positive and negative halves
Leave the crystal whole and electrically neutral

questions.question: In the equation NaCl(s) → Na⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq), the label aq means the ion is:
options: Dissolved in water, swimming with its water escort
Stuck to the bottom as a solid

questions.question: Salt water lights the detective's bulb because:
options: Salt turns water into a metal
Salt water is warmer than plain water
Free-swimming ions ferry the current across the glass
The battery works harder in salty water

questions.question: A dark bulb proves:
options: Only that nothing charged is swimming in the liquid — not that nothing dissolved
That the liquid is pure water
That the solution is completely saturated

questions.question: The brightness of the bulb keeps score of:
options: The colour of the dissolved substance
The concentration of ions in the solution

questions.question: Sports drinks advertise electrolytes because the human body:
options: Runs nerves and muscles on ion traffic, and sweating drains ions away
Needs sugar for its nerve signals

subtopics.title: Snow in a Glass — and Naming the Mystery Ion

questions.question: Golden snow falls when lead nitrate and potassium iodide solutions mix because:
options: The potassium and nitrate ions form a yellow solid
The water turns yellow with heat
Lead and iodide ions pair into insoluble yellow lead iodide
The glass reacts with the lead

questions.question: The opening splash of dilute nitric acid in every ion test acts as:
options: A lie detector — it fizzes away carbonate so it cannot fake another ion's snow
A brightener for the precipitate colours
A way to dissolve the silver nitrate

questions.question: The halide colour code with silver nitrate reads:
options: Yellow chloride, cream iodide, white bromide
All three halides give the same white
Red chloride, orange bromide, green iodide
White chloride, cream bromide, yellow iodide

questions.question: Partner-swap reaction families differ from redox because in a partner swap:
options: Every ion keeps its charge, while redox changes atoms' charges
The reaction only works when heated
